options.doc: The API the picks build: `rest` | `graphql`. Default: `rest`.

choices.doc: a JSON API with OpenApiSpex documentation
an Absinthe schema and resolvers

need.line: Your project is vanilla and the shelf is full: you want the workbench's own picks in, without choosing box by box.
need.body:
Your project is vanilla and the shelf is full: you want the workbench's own picks in, without choosing box by box.

**Before:** a stock `phx.new` project boots in the workbench, and every capability is a decision — which API, which docs, which coverage, which checks — made ten times, in the right order, every time you start something.

**After:** one box inserts the chief's picks — the dep-only quintet, REST or GraphQL as you say, coveralls, the ExDoc site, the enhancements base and the healthcheck endpoint — each as its own commit, so `eject` still takes any one of them out alone.

**Not for:** a project that wants its own combination — the picks are fixed on purpose: if you would uncheck one, skip the box and add cartridges à la carte. A member's fine options (coverage theme, probe path) are set on the member, never here.

cartridges.summary: Outfits the project with the chief's picks

cartridges.name: ansi

need.line: You read the application's logs through Docker, and everything comes out the same shade of grey.
need.body:
You read the application's logs through Docker, and everything comes out the same shade of grey.

**Before:** Elixir sees no terminal on the other side of the container and turns colour off, so the `[info]` and the `[error]` look alike in a wall of output.

**After:** one line in `config.exs`, and the levels, the SQL and the stack traces come out coloured wherever you read them — `./wb.sh logs`, `iex`, the console.

**Not for:** colouring what the runtime does not colour already; it lifts Elixir's own decision, it does not add formatting.

cartridges.summary: Turns ANSI colours back on for logs read outside a terminal

cartridges.name: toolchain

options.name: elixir
options.doc: Elixir version. Default: the one running the installer.

options.name: erlang
options.doc: Erlang/OTP version. Default: the one running the installer.

need.line: You open the project in your editor, on your own machine, and nothing there knows which Elixir this is.
need.body:
You open the project in your editor, on your own machine, and nothing there knows which Elixir this is.

**Before:** the container has the right stack and your host has whatever it has; the language server picks the wrong version, `mix` in your shell disagrees with `./wb.sh mix`, and `.elixir_ls/` keeps showing up in `git status`.

**After:** a `.tool-versions` naming the Elixir and Erlang the workspace actually runs — read straight off the toolchain that installs it, so it cannot drift — and the language server's cache ignored by git.

**Not for:** the container, which takes its stack from the image and never reads this file; and not for `mix.exs`, whose `elixir:` line is a requirement range, not a pin.

cartridges.summary: Pins the Elixir and Erlang the project runs on, for the host

cartridges.name: versioning

options.name: version
options.doc: Version the project starts at, in `mix.exs` and the changelog. Default: `0.0.0`.

need.line: You are about to change something, and there is nowhere to say what changed.
need.body:
You are about to change something, and there is nowhere to say what changed.

**Before:** the version is `0.1.0` because the generator had to write something, and the history of the project is its git log — which records every commit and answers no question a reader has.

**After:** a version the project chose, and a `CHANGELOG.md` opened at it: an `Unreleased` section to write into as you go, and a template line to uncomment when you cut the release.

**Not for:** bumping the version for you — deciding when `0.1.0` becomes `0.2.0` is the one part of this that cannot be automated.

cartridges.summary: Sets the project's initial version and opens its changelog

cartridges.name: osmon

need.line: You want the machine's CPU, memory and disk where you already look.
need.body:
You want the machine's CPU, memory and disk where you already look.

**Before:** `top` in another terminal.

**After:** `:os_mon` feeding LiveDashboard's OS page.

**Not for:** application metrics — those are telemetry's, and already on the dashboard.

cartridges.summary: Enables the :os_mon OTP application for system monitoring

cartridges.name: psql_extras

need.line: Your Postgres is slow, and you don't know which query.
need.body:
Your Postgres is slow, and you don't know which query.

**Before:** guessing from the logs.

**After:** ready-made diagnostics — unused indexes, locks, the slowest queries, cache hit rates — from `iex` or the dashboard.

**Not for:** other databases — it reads Postgres's own statistics.

cartridges.summary: Adds ecto_psql_extras database insights to the project

cartridges.name: credo

need.line: You want a reviewer that never gets tired of the same remarks.
need.body:
You want a reviewer that never gets tired of the same remarks.

**Before:** style and smell debates in every review, by hand.

**After:** `mix credo` flags them before they land, with the project's own configuration.

**Not for:** bugs — it reads style and structure, not behaviour.

cartridges.summary: Adds Credo static code analysis to the project

cartridges.name: mock

need.line: Your tests must not call the real service.
need.body:
Your tests must not call the real service.

**Before:** tests that reach an API, or code that is untestable because it does.

**After:** `Mock` stubs a module for the duration of a test.

**Not for:** OTP 29 and later — `meck` does not compile there; the migration to Mox is pending.

cartridges.summary: Adds the Mock testing library to the project

cartridges.name: exdebug

need.line: You want to look at a value while developing without dressing it up first.
need.body:
You want to look at a value while developing without dressing it up first.

**Before:** `IO.inspect` with a label, again, and cleaning them up afterwards.

**After:** ExDebug's helpers for inspecting values comfortably, from a terminal or a test.

**Not for:** production — it is a development aid.

cartridges.summary: Adds the ExDebug utility to the project

need.line: Other systems will talk to your app, and need a contract to do it.
need.body:
Other systems will talk to your app, and need a contract to do it.

**Before:** routes without a spec, documented by reading the controllers.

**After:** `/api/v1` as the home of every endpoint, an OpenAPI spec kept beside the code, SwaggerUI at `/dev/swagger`.

**Not for:** alongside `graphql` — one interface per project.

cartridges.summary: Adds OpenAPI (open_api_spex) REST documentation to the project

cartridges.name: graphql

need.line: Your clients want to ask for exactly the data they need, and nothing more.
need.body:
Your clients want to ask for exactly the data they need, and nothing more.

**Before:** many fixed endpoints, each deciding the shape of its answer.

**After:** one endpoint backed by an Absinthe schema, `/graphiql` to explore it, and clients composing their own queries.

**Not for:** alongside `rest` — one interface per project.

cartridges.summary: Adds an Absinthe GraphQL API served at /graphiql to the project

the GraphQL project: nothing skipped

the original workbench report

need.line: You want to know where the tests aren't looking.
need.body:
You want to know where the tests aren't looking.

**Before:** a green suite and no idea which lines it never touched.

**After:** `mix cover`: a percentage, an HTML report — at `/dev/docs/cover` with exdoc — and a minimum the build can refuse to go under.

**Not for:** proving the code is right — coverage says where the tests are, not whether they ask the right questions.

cartridges.summary: Adds ExCoveralls test coverage reports to the project
cartridges.afterwards: ./wb.sh mix cover runs the suite and writes the report; --build does it on the insert.

need.line: You want the project's documentation readable, served by the project itself.
need.body:
You want the project's documentation readable, served by the project itself.

**Before:** module and function docs nobody opens, and the curated pages nowhere.

**After:** `/dev/docs`: ExDoc's site built from the code, plus the workbench's pages — coverage, the auth token, the database diagram — one URL away in dev.

**Not for:** publishing — it is served in dev; HexDocs is another step.

cartridges.summary: Adds ExDoc documentation served at /dev/docs to the project
cartridges.afterwards: ./wb.sh mix docs generates the site; --build does it on the insert.

cartridges.name: guidelines

options.name: url
options.doc: URL of the markdown to download as the project's coding guidelines page.

need.line: Your team agreed how it writes Elixir, and the agreement lives somewhere nobody opens.
need.body:
Your team agreed how it writes Elixir, and the agreement lives somewhere nobody opens.

**Before:** the conventions are a link in a wiki, or in another repository's README: the people who most need them — whoever joined last week — never find them, and reviews re-litigate the same commas.

**After:** the guide is a page of the project's own documentation, beside the modules it talks about, at `/dev/docs` with everything else.

**Not for:** enforcing anything — that is [credo](../credo/)'s job. This puts the text where it is read; nothing checks the code against it.

cartridges.summary: Adds the team's coding conventions to the project's docs

need.line: You want the workbench's house conventions in the project from day one.
need.body:
You want the workbench's house conventions in the project from day one.

**Before:** every project deciding its schema base, its helper, its tasks and its first tests on its own.

**After:** `MyApp.Schema`, the helper, `mix db` and `mix version`, and a base test suite that already covers what the setup wired.

**Not for:** the vanilla line — this is the opinionated line's foundation, and `new2` leaves the project stock.

cartridges.summary: Adds the workbench base enhancements (helper, schema, tasks, tests)

need.line: Your app needs users who sign in, and you never want to hold a password.
need.body:
Your app needs users who sign in, and you never want to hold a password.

**Before:** rolling your own authentication, or storing password hashes and everything that follows from it.

**After:** Auth0 does identity and issues JWTs; the project gets an Accounts context, a User and a token plug, and never sees a password.

**Not for:** new projects on the vanilla line — the dependencies it rests on are abandoned upstream (config.conf says so); `ash` with `--auth` is the living alternative.

cartridges.summary: Adds Auth0 JWT authentication with an Accounts context to the project

options.name: interface
options.doc: `rest` | `graphql` | `none`. Default: `rest`.

choices.doc: a JSON controller and its OpenAPI schema
an Absinthe schema and resolvers

need.line: You want an assistant inside the product, that remembers each user's conversations.
need.body:
You want an assistant inside the product, that remembers each user's conversations.

**Before:** a chatbot bolted on the side, with no memory and no owner.

**After:** conversations and messages persisted per user, replies from OpenAI's chat models, as a feature of the app.

**Not for:** projects without users — it implies `auth0`.

cartridges.summary: Adds an OpenAI assistant with conversations to the project

cartridges.name: healthcheck

options.name: endpoint
options.doc: Route for the healthcheck scope. Defaults to `/health`.

options.name: open_api
options.doc: Generate the OpenApiSpex-documented variant even if the REST feature is not detected (it must be installed for it to compile).

need.line: Your teammates and your monitoring want to ask the app how it is.
need.body:
Your teammates and your monitoring want to ask the app how it is.

**Before:** logging into the server to find out.

**After:** a public JSON route that answers at once — versions, environment and database details in dev, and an entry in the Swagger page.

**Not for:** an orchestrator's probes — for those, `healthcheck2`, which answers a probe and gets out of the way.

cartridges.summary: Adds a healthcheck endpoint with controller, tests and router scope

need.line: Your users should be able to pay — not done yet.
need.body:
Your users should be able to pay — not done yet.

**Before:** nothing: a manifest and these papers, with no installer
behind them.

**After:** nothing yet: `./wb.sh add stripe` refuses, naming the box.

**Not for:** anything, until it is done.

cartridges.name: githooks

need.line: You want the checks to run before the commit exists, not after the push.
need.body:
You want the checks to run before the commit exists, not after the push.

**Before:** CI catching what a pre-commit hook would have, one push later.

**After:** `git_hooks` running format, tests and credo on commit, configured in the project.

**Not for:** enforcing anything on others — hooks are local to each clone.

cartridges.summary: Adds git_hooks management to the project

cartridges.name: exmachina

need.line: Your tests need realistic records, in one line each.
need.body:
Your tests need realistic records, in one line each.

**Before:** hand-built maps and inserts repeated in every test.

**After:** ExMachina factories: `insert(:user)` with sensible defaults, overridable.

**Not for:** production data — factories are for tests.

cartridges.summary: Adds ExMachina test factories to the project

cartridges.name: clustering

options.name: dns_query
options.doc: Value for `DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY`, the DNS name that resolves to the replica IPs. Defaults to `<app>.default.svc.cluster.local` (Kubernetes); on Fly.io it is usually `<app>.internal`.

need.line: Your deployment runs several replicas, and they should act as one.
need.body:
Your deployment runs several replicas, and they should act as one.

**Before:** replicas that never see each other: a PubSub per node, a broadcast that reaches one browser in four.

**After:** the release boots as a named node from its own address and `DNSCluster` finds the others through one DNS name; `./wb.sh up --deploy scaled` shows four of them join.

**Not for:** a single workspace — one container has nothing to cluster with; and rolling deploys across images, since the cookie is baked.

cartridges.summary: Boots the production release as a distributed node for DNSCluster
cartridges.afterwards: See it work: ./wb.sh up --deploy scaled brings the replicas up behind the balancer (the release image is rebuilt on each deploy).

cartridges.name: healthcheck2

options.name: path
options.doc: Prefix of the two probe routes. Defaults to `/health` (`/health/live` and `/health/ready`).

need.line: Your platform polls the app, and the answer decides whether it restarts it or diverts traffic.
need.body:
Your platform polls the app, and the answer decides whether it restarts it or diverts traffic.

**Before:** one route answering both questions the same way — restarting on a database outage, or passing a probe through a redirect.

**After:** `/health/live` and `/health/ready` as the first plug of the endpoint: alive if the VM answers, ready if the repo does, within a second.

**Not for:** humans reading a body — it says `ok` or `unavailable`; the JSON is `healthcheck`'s.

cartridges.summary: Adds liveness and readiness probes as the first plug of the endpoint

need.line: You want a whole framework for your domain, set up the way its own site does it.
need.body:
You want a whole framework for your domain, set up the way its own site does it.

**Before:** reading Ash's guides and running a chain of installers by hand, in an order one of them hangs on when it is wrong.

**After:** `--data-layer`, `--api`, `--auth`, `--with`: the command ash-hq.org's installer generates for an existing app, queued and run; `mix workbench.ash.site` tells you when the site's map moved.

**Not for:** the opinionated line (`new`) — its `users` table and generators fight with Ash's domain; this is a `new2` cartridge.

cartridges.summary: Installs the Ash framework, configured like ash-hq.org's installer for an existing app
cartridges.afterwards: With a database data layer on a project born without Ecto, ./wb.sh bake puts the database into the workspace's compose, then ./wb.sh setup creates it.

cartridges.name: mailer

need.line: You want to see the mail your app sends before anyone else does.
need.body:
You want to see the mail your app sends before anyone else does.

**Before:** a real SMTP account wired into dev, or `IO.inspect` on the email struct; a mail that leaves for a real address from a laptop.

**After:** every mail delivered in dev lands in `/dev/mailbox`, open in the browser; tests assert on it through the `Test` adapter; production sends through the adapter you configure in `runtime.exs`.

**Not for:** choosing a provider — that is your account and one config line, and `phx.new` leaves it as a comment.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix's Swoosh mailer, as phx.new would have generated it

cartridges.name: gettext

need.line: Your users don't all read English, and the strings are already written.
need.body:
Your users don't all read English, and the strings are already written.

**Before:** strings hard-coded in the components and layouts; a second language means touching every template, and a missing translation shows nothing.

**After:** every string `phx.new` wrote is a `gettext` call with the English as its own fallback; a locale is a `.po` file under `priv/gettext`; `mix gettext.extract` finds the strings you add once you wrap them.

**Not for:** translating for you — your own strings still have to be wrapped, and the locale files still have to be filled in.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix's gettext, as phx.new would have generated it

cartridges.name: ecto

options.name: database
options.doc: The database adapter, as `phx.new --database` names them: `postgres` (default), `mysql`, `mssql`, `sqlite3`. The workspace's compose provides a Postgres; SQLite needs none.

choices.doc: via postgrex — the one the workspace's compose provides
via myxql — no service in the workspace's compose
via tds — no service in the workspace's compose
via ecto_sqlite3 — a file, no service needed

options.name: binary_id
options.doc: `binary_id` as the primary key type of the Ecto schemas the generators make (`phx.new --binary-id`): the `generators` entry of `config.exs`.

need.line: Your app has data to keep, and it started without a database.
need.body:
Your app has data to keep, and it started without a database.

**Before:** an API that computes and forgets, or a repo wired by hand across four config files and a supervision tree, with the tests sharing one database.

**After:** a `Repo` on the adapter you name, migrations under `priv/repo`, the sandbox that isolates every test, `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`, and the workspace's Postgres after `./wb.sh bake`.

**Not for:** changing your mind later — a project with data changes database by migration, not by flag; inserted once.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix's Ecto with a database adapter, as phx.new would have generated it
cartridges.afterwards: ./wb.sh bake puts the database into the workspace's compose, then ./wb.sh setup creates it.

cartridges.name: esbuild

need.line: Your page needs JavaScript, and there is no bundler to write it in.
need.body:
Your page needs JavaScript, and there is no bundler to write it in.

**Before:** a placeholder `app.js` that is a comment telling you which scripts to copy by hand; no `import`, no LiveView client, no watcher.

**After:** `assets/js/app.js` bundled on every save, `phoenix_html` and `phoenix_live_view` a plain `import` away, one file to ship with `mix assets.deploy`.

**Not for:** a Node toolchain — esbuild's binary comes alone; npm packages are a choice you make afterwards.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix's esbuild JavaScript bundling, as phx.new would have generated it

cartridges.name: tailwind

need.line: Your markup was written for Tailwind, and a frozen stylesheet is styling it.
need.body:
Your markup was written for Tailwind, and a frozen stylesheet is styling it.

**Before:** classes in every template that mean nothing, an 80 kB `default.css` snapshot that never changes, no theme, no icons.

**After:** the classes come alive, rebuilt on save; heroicons as CSS classes, daisyUI's components, a light/dark/system toggle in the layout.

**Not for:** a project without html — the build needs LiveView's compiler, which html brings; the insert says so.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix's Tailwind CSS pipeline, as phx.new would have generated it

cartridges.name: html

need.line: Your API needs a page.
need.body:
Your API needs a page.

**Before:** JSON only: no layouts, no components, no browser pipeline, and `phx.gen.html` generating files that cannot compile.

**After:** `/` with a home page, a root layout and `Layouts.app`, the core components, HTML error pages, the browser pipeline with session and CSRF, live reload — the page a `phx.new` project is born with.

**Not for:** LiveView — that is `live`, on top of this; and styling, which is `tailwind`.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix's HTML views, as phx.new would have generated them

cartridges.name: live

need.line: Your page should react without reloading.
need.body:
Your page should react without reloading.

**Before:** html with its `LiveSocket` lines written but commented out; every click a full request; no `phx-click`, no JS commands.

**After:** the `/live` socket connected on load, `phx-click` on the flash and the theme toggle, `show`/`hide` commands, a LiveView mountable from the router.

**Not for:** a project without esbuild — the client lives in `app.js`, and without a bundler there is nothing in the browser to connect; the insert says so.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix LiveView, as phx.new would have generated it

cartridges.name: dashboard

need.line: Something is slow in dev and you're guessing.
need.body:
Something is slow in dev and you're guessing.

**Before:** logs, `:observer` if you remember how to start it, a hunch about which process it is.

**After:** `/dev/dashboard` — processes, memory, ETS, every request timed, the repo's queries when there is one — live in the browser, on the `/live` socket, only in dev.

**Not for:** production monitoring — it has no authentication and stays behind `dev_routes`.

cartridges.summary: Adds Phoenix LiveDashboard, as phx.new would have generated it
